## Fleet tag ordering and assignment UX

- Fleet → Groups now stages tag-order edits and sends one atomic Save instead
  of writing after every drag. The editor presents Total, contiguous namespace
  groups, and exact tags as an expandable hierarchy; groups and exact tags are
  independently draggable, Revert restores the saved order, and browser-local
  expansion state keeps large exact-tag lists out of the way by default.
- A fleet-wide natural-order policy can normalize tags inside each namespace
  group, including tags created later. One-shot per-group sorting remains
  available when the policy is off. Group order itself remains operator-owned.
- Tag creation, assignment, identity import, deletion, and reorder now share
  one serialized ordering model in Memory and PostgreSQL, including safe
  reconciliation when a new tag arrives while an operator has a staged draft.
- Fleet → Assignments now performs the required preview/hash confirmation for
  remove and undo. In both Assignments and expanded Instances, clicking a tag
  label is inert and only the accessible × button removes it.

## Monitoring and VPS details

- Inline and canonical VPS detail add a System section for the already-reported
  OS, CPU model, kernel, architecture, and virtualization facts. Current swap
  use is shown with resource facts, and retained private resource history adds
  a Swap-used series when swap evidence exists.
- Fleet Monitor and Shared views add an explicit Name sort. Warnings-first now
  uses name and stable VPS identity as its tie-breaker instead of live
  throughput or CPU, so equally healthy cards no longer reshuffle with traffic.
- Comfortable cards retain the country flag wherever the operator preference
  or shared identity visibility allows it. Uptime evidence is described as
  “Up since …”, and non-total traffic selectors label card quota summaries as
  RX, TX, or Max while preserving the existing limiting-quota calculation.
- These are presentation changes over existing monitoring evidence; no new
  system-information or swap telemetry is disclosed through public shares.

## Deployment backup command

- `./update.sh backup` creates an immediate, transactionally consistent live
  PostgreSQL custom archive under `runtime/update-backups/` without stopping
  application services. It shares the updater lock, validates with
  `pg_restore --list`, publishes atomically with mode `0600`, and never
  overwrites an existing same-name archive.
- The command is database-only, local, unencrypted, and unpruned. It does not
  replace the documented encrypted off-host backup of configuration, secrets,
  object data, and the database.

## API and database compatibility

- `/api/v1/tags/order` now supports GET and returns
  `{tags, namespace_natural_sort_enabled}`. PUT requires
  `{ordered_tags, namespace_natural_sort_enabled}` and returns that same state
  object; external consumers of the earlier array-only PUT contract must
  update.
- Migration `0009_fleet_tag_settings.sql` adds the expandable key/value store
  used by the fleet-wide tag-order policy. A database with the exact v0.3.5
  `0001`–`0008` migrations may apply `0009` in place; existing tags and display
  order are preserved and namespace natural sorting initializes disabled.
  Migrations `0001`–`0008` are byte-identical to v0.3.5; earlier or different
  canonical baselines remain subject to the documented
  fresh-database/export-import compatibility rule.
- After `0009` is applied, rollback to v0.3.5 requires restoring the complete
  pre-upgrade database and deployment backup. The updater does not reverse
  database migrations.
